newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo set for 10-day Asian trip to broaden trade.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo set for 10-day Asian trip to broaden trade.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo was set to travel to Asia this week in a bid to extend his country's trade reach beyond its giant northern neighbor and drum up investment for his country's struggling economy.
Zedillo will visit China, South Korea, Singapore and the Phillipines during a 10-day trip beginning on Wednesday. His visit to South Korea will be the first ever by a Mexican head of state.

A highlight of the trip was expected to be the annual summit of the Asian Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) on Nov. 25 in Manila, where Zedillo was expected to tout Mexico's recovery from the 1994 peso crash.

After he took power in 1994, Zedillo charted an economic course of export-driven growth through a competitive peso in a bid to mirror Asia's economic success. Mexico's economy was slowly growing after a deep recession due in part to exports.

But Mexico's trade is tied almost exclusively to the United States with whom Mexico has a free-trade accord. Of Mexico's $76 billion in annual two-way trade with APEC, some $70 billion is accounted for by the United States.

"Trade diversification is an issue that will be present throughout the president's trip to Asia," Juan Rebolledo, assistant secretary for foreign affairs, told reporters on Monday during a briefing about the trip.
Zedillo will arrive in Beijing late on Thursday and was to meet President Jiang Zemin during a three-day visit that also includes a visit to Shanghai on Nov. 24, officials said.

After the APEC meeting, the president travels to Singapore for a two-day visit before heading to South Korea on Nov. 28. Zedillo will stay in South Korea for four days and meet with President Kim Young-sam and Korea's top business leaders.
Mexico was expected to sign a few diplomatic protocol agreements with China as well as an anti-drugs cooperation accord.
